sections.scene: In low orbit above a blue planet, <Subject 1>, an astronaut in a practical white EVA suit, is tethered outside a damaged research station while a loose equipment case drifts away.
sections.shot_list: 0.00-1.30s: establish the astronaut, station hull and drifting case. 1.30-3.40s: <Subject 1> fires one short maneuvering burst and reaches along the tether. 3.40s-end: the glove catches the case handle and rotation settles.
sections.acting: Movement is slow and inertial. The torso reacts after each thruster burst, the tether stays under tension and the catch transfers momentum through the arm.
sections.light_and_image: Unfiltered orbital sunlight, deep black space, controlled visor reflections, detailed suit fabric and physically plausible Earth bounce light.
sections.camera: One stabilized exterior tracking move parallel to the hull with subtle orbital drift; preserve orientation and never cut.
sections.production_sound: Inside-suit breathing, radio compression, short thruster impulses, tether vibration and muted glove contact; exterior space remains silent.
sections.non_diegetic_music: A restrained high string harmonic enters during the reach and resolves on the catch.
sections.negatives: No gravity-like falling, no flapping cloth, no changing station geometry, no extra limbs, no visor face drift, no lens flare overload, no text.
